entry.title: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma Denies Sale Rumors Amid Restructuring
entry.content:
Techmeme | nytimes.com

Asha Sharma, who was appointed CEO of Xbox without prior experience in the video game industry, is defending the brand's long-term viability. Despite significant layoffs and the divestment of several studios under her leadership, Sharma maintains that the Xbox division is not for sale.

The restructuring effort aims to restore the division's core fundamentals and stabilize operating margins. These changes come amid increased industry speculation that Microsoft may consider spinning off its gaming business.

entry.title: Grasshopper Manufacture Splits From NetEase to Become Independent
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com | source

Grasshopper Manufacture is splitting from parent company NetEase Games to operate as an independent developer. CEO Goichi Suda stated the decision follows the completion of the action-adventure game Romeo Is A Dead Man and is intended to allow the studio to pursue a wider variety of game styles.

The studio, which developed the No More Heroes series, has been a subsidiary of NetEase since 2021 and was previously under the GungHo Group. Grasshopper Manufacture plans to utilize its increased self-publishing capabilities to maintain its signature "NO GAME NO LIFE" brand through various publishing models.

entry.title: Ubisoft Montreal Employees Launch Petition to Preserve Hybrid Work
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com | source

Workers represented by the Ubisoft Workers of Montreal union have launched a petition to protest a mandatory five-day in-office policy and protect hybrid work schedules. The campaign has gathered over 300 signatures through in-person and digital collection.

The movement follows Ubisoft's January restructuring, which included return-to-office mandates, layoffs, and studio closures. Similar labor unrest has previously occurred among Ubisoft's Paris-based employees.

entry.title: Factorio Quality Upcycling: Mathematical Model and Calculator
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | exyr.org | hacker news

Mathematical modeling using transition matrices and linear equations allows for the calculation of quality transitions in the *Factorio: Space Age* expansion. This approach specifically addresses "washing" (pure recycling loops) and "upcycling" (crafting-recycling cycles) to predict how items move through different quality tiers.

An online calculator tool is provided to help players forecast resource consumption and output rates for high-quality items. The model incorporates variables such as module probabilities, recycling ingredient returns, and recipe productivity bonuses.

entry.title: Valve to Transition Steam's Discounts and Events Tab to Personalized Algorithms
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com | source

Valve is transitioning Steam's "Discounts and Events" tab from a manual, calendar-based system to an algorithm-driven recommendation engine. This shift aims to increase game discoverability by presenting personalized content tailored to individual users. Preliminary testing showed the personalized model displayed ten times more games daily, which increased store page visits, wishlists, and cart additions.

The transition is expected to reach full implementation by early 2027, following a current pause on new manual curated placements. The change is intended to benefit smaller developers by reducing the need for manual scheduling or direct curation by Valve staff. Industry feedback suggests the shift can drive significant traffic to niche titles that previously had minimal visibility on the curated page.

entry.title: Mikael Kasurinen Explains Decision to Avoid Yellow Paint in Control Resonant
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com | source

Following the launch of Remedy Entertainment's Control Resonant, director Mikael Kasurinen explained the studio's decision to eschew common visual shorthand for player guidance in favor of organic environmental cues. This design choice aims to enhance player agency, ensuring players feel they have discovered paths themselves rather than following dictated routes. In the game's gravity-shifting Manhattan, navigation is guided by subtle elements like wind and rain direction instead of explicit color-coded markers.

The choice addresses industry-wide debate over "handholding" mechanics intended to reduce player frustration. Kasurinen argues that excessive signposting can disrupt the horror-inspired theme of interpreting an unknowable reality. By relying on environmental subtlety, the developers aim to make navigation an active part of the player experience.

entry.title: Embark Studios Executive Discusses Burnout Caused by Arc Raiders Live Service Demands
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com

Aleksander Grøndal, Executive Producer at Embark Studios, stated that the high content demands of the live service game Arc Raiders led to widespread employee burnout. To address the tension between player expectations and workforce capacity, the studio moved away from a monthly update schedule to prioritize quality and long-term sustainability.

The shift follows a period where developers struggled to balance rapid content production with the heavy maintenance required for a live-service title. Grøndal emphasized that creating frameworks for work-life balance is essential to retaining the creative talent necessary for the game's long-term success.

entry.title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella Calls Xbox Layoffs 'Streamlining'
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com | source

Microsoft has cut at least 5,750 jobs through five rounds of layoffs since the October 2023 acquisition of Activision Blizzard, a process CEO Satya Nadella has characterized as "streamlining" the Xbox division. The most recent round, confirmed in July 2026, involves 3,200 roles within Xbox Game Studios and includes the divestment of studios such as Double Fine, Compulsion Games, and Undead Labs.

This restructuring follows a leadership transition to new Xbox head Asha Sharma and occurs amidst declining hardware revenue and a component shortage driven by AI datacenter demand. While Nadella expressed confidence in the company's intellectual property and projected growth for the upcoming fiscal year, affected developers have warned that the loss of specialized talent could disrupt complex production pipelines.

entry.title: Steam Beta Introduces Pyrowave Experimental Video Codec for Low-Latency Streaming
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | phoronix.com | source | discussion

Valve has added Pyrowave, an experimental video codec, to the Steam client beta for Windows, macOS, and Linux. Developed by Hans-Kristian Arntzen, the codec is designed for high-bandwidth, low-latency video streaming, specifically targeting local network usage over Gigabit Ethernet.

Pyrowave utilizes the Vulkan API and supports HDR and YUV 4:4:4 color formats. Because it requires 5 to 10 times more bandwidth than existing streaming codecs, it is optimized for high-performance LAN environments. The feature is accessible through the Steam Remote Play advanced client settings in the beta versions.

entry.title: Rustunit Removes Swift Package Dependencies from Bevy iOS Crates
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | rustunit.com | discussion

Rustunit has updated its `bevy_ios_*` crates to replace manual Swift package dependencies with direct `objc2` bindings. This allows developers to install necessary iOS functionality, such as safe area insets and user notifications, using only `cargo add`, removing the requirement for the Swift Package Manager (SPM).

This transition simplifies version management between Rust crates and SPM packages and enables builds for the iOS simulator. While most functionality now uses the Objective-C runtime via `objc2`, `bevy_ios_iap` utilizes a minimal, statically linked Swift shim to accommodate the Swift-only StoreKit 2 API.
